report.summary: Chunk 4 of attempt.py: defines _GIT_INHERITED_CONFIG, _inherited_config_args, _git_env, and _git. Claims about config inheritance, git environment sanitization, and process-launch attacks are partially checkable; several cross-references are uncheckable.
risks: _inherited_config_args | medium | Silent failure on config read may skip inheritance; code comments say this is intentional and safe. | Verify by test that exceptions are indeed caught and ignored.

_git_env | high | Environment sanitization is critical for security; any missed leaky variable could allow filter injection. | Audit list of popped variables against git documentation for all config-inheriting environment variables.

_git | critical | The function is the single choke point for git execution; the docstring claims it prevents writes to primary checkout via PrimaryCheckoutWrite, but the implementation is not fully visible in this chunk. | Verify that _overlap_reason and PrimaryCheckoutWrite are correctly implemented and that the check covers all write verbs.

_git | critical | The docstring describes a filter attack scenario; the defense relies on --git-dir/--work-tree, _git_env, and _GIT_EXEC_CONFIG. The last is not defined in this chunk. | Confirm that _GIT_EXEC_CONFIG is defined and applied via -c in _git.
todos: Confirm that _GIT_EXEC_CONFIG is defined and used in _git.
Verify that _overlap_reason and PrimaryCheckoutWrite are implemented correctly.
Audit the list of popped environment variables in _git_env for completeness.
Add tests for _inherited_config_args to ensure silent failure does not cause issues.
Ensure that the filter attack scenario is fully mitigated with all three properties.

handoff.purpose: Define git configuration inheritance, environment sanitization, and the single git execution choke point.

symbols.name: _GIT_INHERITED_CONFIG
symbols.note: Tuple of git config keys inherited from the operator's real environment.

symbols.name: _inherited_config_args
symbols.note: Reads allowlisted config keys from git using _git with harden=False, returns tuple of -c arguments. Cached. Silent on failure.

symbols.name: _git_env
symbols.note: Returns a sanitized environment dict for git subprocesses, removes system/user config and leaky variables.

symbols.name: _git
symbols.note: Single choke point for git execution. Enforces read-only check for primary checkout, returns raw bytes. Hardens environment and applies exec config.

claims.text: Read the allowlisted keys from the operator's REAL config, once.
claims.why: Code calls _git(['config', '--get', key], ...) which reads the actual git config.

claims.text: Read with git's ordinary environment on purpose: the question is what this checkout was created under, and the answer lives in the config the hardened environment is about to hide.
claims.why: The function is called before _git_env is applied; it uses default environment by passing harden=False (implied default? Actually harden default is True, but call passes harden=False explicitly).

claims.text: Cached because it cannot change mid-run and the alternative is a subprocess per key per git call.

Failure is silent BY DESIGN and is the safe direction: a key we cannot read is simply not passed, which leaves git's own default. The dangerous direction would be inheriting something we did not mean to.
claims.why: The try/except with bare 'continue' silently skips on any exception.

claims.text: The environment git is spawned with: no config it did not get from us.
claims.why: Function sets GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL to devnull, and removes leaky variables.

claims.text: GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM and an empty GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL remove the system and per-user config files from the lookup, which is where a filter.* definition would otherwise live.

On this box that is not hypothetical -- git config --list --show-origin shows filter.lfs.* in BOTH the system and the user config, so a candidate that writes * filter=lfs into .gitattributes makes git add spawn git-lfs with no config of its own at all.
claims.why: This is an anecdotal observation about a specific box; no code in this chunk verifies that claim.

claims.text: GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF and friends are dropped rather than emptied: an empty value for some of these is a *valid command*, not an absence.
claims.why: Code uses env.pop(key, None) which removes the key entirely, not setting to empty string.

claims.text: Run git and return the RAW BYTES it produced.
claims.why: Function returns subprocess.CompletedProcess; no decoding is performed in this chunk.

claims.text: The single choke point (see the module docstring).
claims.why: The module docstring is not in this chunk; cannot verify that _git is the only place git is called.

claims.text: cwd inside the primary checkout is restricted to READ_ONLY_REPO_VERBS; anything else raises PrimaryCheckoutWrite before the process is spawned.
claims.why: The chunk shows the check for verb not in READ_ONLY_REPO_VERBS and then calls _overlap_reason; but the definition of READ_ONLY_REPO_VERBS and the exception are not in this chunk. The logic is present but incomplete.

claims.text: Output is not decoded: a patch digest must be taken over the bytes git emitted, so a lossy decode can never change what was hashed.
claims.why: No decoding is done in this chunk; raw bytes are returned.

claims.text: GIT IS A PROCESS LAUNCHER, AND THE CANDIDATE CHOOSES WHAT IT LAUNCHES. This was measured on this box (git 2.38.1.windows.1), not reasoned about.
claims.why: This is an anecdotal claim about a specific git version; no code in this chunk verifies the attack.

claims.text: <worktree>/.gitattributes is plain candidate content; it selects a filter.<name>.clean program, and git add -A runs it.
claims.why: This describes a hypothetical attack; no code in this chunk demonstrates it.

claims.text: In a probe reproducing this module's exact call shape the spawned program executed and wrote its marker, and git add returned 0 with empty stderr. Worse, the two follow-up diffs also returned 0 and produced ~1.6 kB of plausible diff, so the attempt continued to STATE_CLEAN and returned an ordinary AttemptResult with no error field. Nothing would have been noticed.
claims.why: This is a detailed description of a specific test; no code in this chunk confirms it.

claims.text: Three properties close it, and all three are needed: 1. --git-dir/--work-tree ON THE COMMAND LINE. 2. _git_env, so the system and user config cannot supply a filter. 3. _GIT_EXEC_CONFIG pinned with -c, which no config file can override, for the keys that name a program directly.
claims.why: Properties 1 and 2 are implemented in this chunk (--git-dir/--work-tree via parameters, _git_env function). Property 3 (_GIT_EXEC_CONFIG) is not defined in this chunk, so its application cannot be verified.

claims.text: WHY NOT CONTAINMENT INSTEAD. This runs in the PARENT process, before the gate, and the plan of containing only the gate leaves it entirely open. The attack also needs only worktree-local writes plus reads, and daedalus.spine.containment states CONFIDENTIALITY: NONE -- a write-contained candidate can still read and still plant these bytes.
claims.why: References to 'gate' and daedalus.spine.containment are outside this chunk.

observations.what: _inherited_config_args calls _git with harden=False, but _git's default harden is True. The call explicitly passes harden=False, which is consistent with the intent to read the real config.
The claim about three properties for security references _GIT_EXEC_CONFIG, but this constant is not defined in this chunk. Its existence and usage are uncheckable.
The docstring for _git_env states it drops GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF and friends, but the list of popped variables includes many more; the claim is accurate but incomplete.
The function _git enforces a read-only check on the primary checkout, but the actual check (_overlap_reason and PrimaryCheckoutWrite) is not fully visible in this chunk.
